The OCJ 'Sept. 3 explicit prohibition' entry is Liberty Township in Knox County (Marta Hill, Knox County Regional Planning Commission), not Wood County.
evidence.quote: Marta Hill represents Liberty Township at the Knox County Regional Planning Commission ... The township passed a resolution explicitly prohibiting data centers Sept. 3

evidence.supports: Wood County's Liberty Township (Rudolph) trustees; no zoning prohibition found.

decisions.notes: OCJ is not wrong, but the packet mis-joined it by name: none of its three 'Liberty Township' ban entries is Wood County. The April and June entries cite LUC Regional Planning (Logan-Union-Champaign) and libertytownshipunionco.com (Union County); the September entry is Knox County per OCJ's own text. No ban or replacement was found for Liberty Township, Wood County. The row stays as it is (news-only moratorium; its existing VERIFY tag still applies).

decisions.notes: OCJ is misfiled for this row. Its 'Council added data centers as prohibited use in September 2025' is the City of Monroe (a council, next to Lemon Township in Butler County). evidence.publisher: Paris Township, Union County (via LUC Regional Planning Commission)
evidence.quote: This version: Amended and restated to reflect amendments adopted April 7, 2026.

evidence.supports: Paris Township adopted a one-year data center moratorium (reported 2026-02-06).

decisions.notes: OCJ describes a different instrument: the 2026-04-07 zoning amendment that defines data centers without permitting them (an effective prohibition, which the row's current_status already notes). No record was found that the trustees lifted or ended the February one-year moratorium, so it is not recorded as 'replaced' and remains nominally in force to about February 2027. If trustee minutes later show the moratorium was ended on adoption of the April amendment, change the status to 'replaced'. Caution for later passes: paris-township.com is Paris Township in PORTAGE County (its minutes cite Shalersville and Portage County Regional Planning), and paristwp.com is Paris Township in STARK County. Neither is this row.

outcome.from: Moratorium plus a city Data Center Moratorium Committee study. Council later rezoned the site (June 2026). Litigation is pending.
outcome.to: Moratorium plus a city Data Center Moratorium Committee study. On 2026-06-16 council unanimously passed Ordinance 4635-26, restoring the pre-2025 zoning text so data centers are no longer a permitted use in the M-1 Light Manufacturing District. The moratorium was not repealed. Litigation is pending, and a charter amendment banning data centers over 7.5 MW is on the November 2026 ballot.
outcome.reason: The row said council 'rezoned the site'; Peak of Ohio reports a text reversal (Ord. 4635-26) removing data centers as a permitted M-1 use, with no repeal of the moratorium.

evidence.supports: Ordinance 4635-26 (2026-06-16) reversed the 2025 amendment that allowed data centers in M-1.
evidence.quote: Council unanimously approved Ordinance 4635-26, restoring the city's zoning code to the version that existed before a 2025 amendment allowed data centers in Urbana's M-1 Light Manufacturing District.

evidence.supports: Thor's appeal of the site plan rejection and 12-month moratorium is still being briefed; the project stays on hold.

decisions.notes: interconnectedcapital overstates this. Ord. 4635-26 removes data centers as a permitted M-1 use; it is not a permanent citywide ban (that is the November ballot charter amendment). It is also a separate instrument from our moratorium, which was not repealed and runs to about 2027-03-03. Status stays active; only the outcome text is corrected.
